name: BESIDE
question: Does adding mirabegron to solifenacin 5 mg improve incontinent overactive bladder after an inadequate response to solifenacin alone?

arms.label: Solifenacin 5 mg plus mirabegron 25–50 mg daily

design.population: 2,174 adults aged at least 18 years with overactive bladder for at least three months and at least two daily incontinence episodes at screening who remained incontinent after four weeks of solifenacin 5 mg daily.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, phase 3b randomized superiority trial

verdictNote: Daily incontinence improved against 5 mg; two key secondary endpoints met noninferiority against 10 mg.
takeaway: After a solifenacin 5 mg run-in, adding mirabegron reduced daily incontinence more than continuing solifenacin 5 mg over 12 weeks (adjusted change −1.80 versus −1.53 episodes; P = 0.001); combination also met noninferiority against solifenacin 10 mg on key secondary endpoints.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Drake MJ, Chapple C, Esen AA, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Mirabegron Add-on Therapy to Solifenacin in Incontinent Overactive Bladder Patients with an Inadequate Response to Initial 4-Week Solifenacin Monotherapy: A Randomised Double-blind Multicentre Phase 3B Study (BESIDE)." *Eur Urol.* 2016;70(1):136-145. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2016.02.030
reports.followUp: 12 weeks of randomized treatment after a 4-week solifenacin run-in

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in episodes per 24 h at 12 weeks; combination versus solifenacin 5 mg
results.note: Adjusted mean difference in episodes per 24 h; rounded arm changes subtract to −0.27.
results.locator: Journal p139 text; p142, Figure 3a; p141 discussion

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in micturitions per 24 h at 12 weeks; combination versus solifenacin 5 mg
results.note: Combination was also noninferior and superior to solifenacin 10 mg on this endpoint; noninferiority margin 0.20 micturitions per 24 h.
results.locator: Journal pp137–139 text; p142, Figure 3b; p141 discussion

results.measure: Incontinence episodes in 3-day diary at 12 weeks; combination versus solifenacin 10 mg
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin: rate ratio 1.11; superiority against 10 mg was not demonstrated. Against 5 mg, combination reduced episodes (P = 0.014).
results.locator: Journal pp137–139 text; p142, Figure 3c; p141 discussion

results.measure: No incontinence episodes at end of treatment
results.note: Effect is combination versus 5 mg; versus 10 mg, OR 1.28 (95% CI 1.02–1.61; P = 0.033).

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in episodes per 24 h at end of treatment
results.note: Effect is mean difference versus 5 mg; adjusted arm values are rounded.

delivery.label: Screening and eligibility
delivery.value: Two-week screening and washout; at least one incontinence episode in a three-day diary required after the four-week solifenacin 5 mg run-in.

delivery.label: Randomized regimen
delivery.value: Four-week single-blind solifenacin 5 mg run-in, then 12-week double-blind solifenacin 5 mg plus mirabegron 25 mg daily (50 mg after week 4), solifenacin 5 mg, or solifenacin 10 mg.

delivery.label: Analysis populations
delivery.value: Randomized: 727/728/719; full analysis set: 707/705/698; safety set: 725/728/719 (combination/5 mg/10 mg).
delivery.locator: Journal pp139–140, Figure 2 and Table 1; p143, Table 3

reports.label: Responder and patient-reported outcomes
reports.citation: MacDiarmid S, Al-Shukri S, Barkin J, et al. "Mirabegron as Add-On Treatment to Solifenacin in Patients with Incontinent Overactive Bladder and an Inadequate Response to Solifenacin Monotherapy: Responder Analyses and Patient-Reported Outcomes from the BESIDE Study [corrected]." *J Urol.* 2016;196(3):809-818. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2016.03.174

results.measure: At least 50% daily incontinence reduction plus at least 10-point OAB-q symptom-bother improvement at 12 weeks
results.note: Exploratory composite responder analysis; OR versus solifenacin 5 mg.

results.measure: Adjusted difference in OAB-q total HRQoL change at 12 weeks

values.exp: 3.15 points greater than ctl5; 3.38 greater than ctl10

results.note: Mean difference versus solifenacin 5 mg; versus 10 mg, 3.38 (95% CI 1.58–5.19; P < 0.001).

reports.label: Cardiovascular safety analysis
reports.citation: Drake MJ, MacDiarmid S, Chapple CR, et al. "Cardiovascular safety in refractory incontinent patients with overactive bladder receiving add-on mirabegron therapy to solifenacin (BESIDE)." *Int J Clin Pract.* 2017;71(5):e12944. doi:10.1111/ijcp.12944
